items.title: AL26-025 - Critical vulnerability impacting BeyondTrust Remote Support – CVE-2026-102764
items.summary:
Number: AL26-025
Date: October 16, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of a critical vulnerability affecting BeyondTrust Remote Support (RS)Footnote 1Footnote 2. In response to the vendor advisory released on October 15, 2026, the Cyber Centre released AV26-1054 on October 16, 2026Footnote 3.

Tracked as CVE-2026-102764Footnote 4, this vulnerability is an Authentication Bypass by Spoofing vulnerability (CWE-290)Footnote 5 that affects all versions of BeyondTrust Remote Support.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to exploit insufficient origin validation in internal BeyondTrust Remote Support messaging components to perform unauthorized file operations on an affected appliance without user interaction. The vulnerability requires no credentials or user action and can enable arbitrary file uploads, potentially resulting in full compromise of the appliance.

The Cyber Centre has observed open-source reporting indicating that the vulnerability is being exploited in the wildFootnote 6.

Suggested actions

The Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations running affected BeyondTrust Remote Support deployments upgrade to the following fixed version:

Affected product Affected versions Fixed versions
BeyondTrust Remote Support Versions 26.2.3 and prior BT26-05-RS patch for versions 24.3.1 to v26.2.3

BeyondTrust has confirmed that a patch addressing this vulnerability was applied to all Remote Support SaaS and Privileged Remote Access SaaS customers as of 9 October 2026. Organizations using these SaaS offerings do not need to take any additional action to remediate this issue.

The Cyber Centre also recommends organizations to:

  • identify BeyondTrust Remote Support deployments within their environments and determine whether they are SaaS-hosted or self-hosted
  • verify the installed Remote Support version. Systems running 26.2.3 or earlier are identified as affected by BeyondTrust
  • upgrade Remote Support installations older than 24.3.1 to a newer supported version before applying the remediation patch
  • apply the BT26-05-RS patch to affected self-hosted Remote Support deployments running versions 24.3.1 through 26.2.3
  • confirm automatic updates are enabled, where appropriate. BeyondTrust specifically advises manual patching for self-hosted instances that are not subscribed to automatic updates
  • as an additional defensive measure, review affected appliances for unexpected or unauthorized file activity, particularly when an appliance was exposed while vulnerable

In addition, the Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations review and implement the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security ActionsFootnote 7 with an emphasis on the following topics:

  • consolidating, monitoring, and defending Internet gateways
  • patch operating systems and applications
  • harden operating systems and applications
  • isolate web-facing applications

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.

items.title: AL26-024 - Critical vulnerabilities affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway – CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 – Update 2
items.summary:
Number: AL26-024
Date: September 27, 2026
Update: October 9, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of critical vulnerabilities affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances. In response to the vendor security bulletin Footnote 1 and blog Footnote 2 released on September 27, 2026, the Cyber Centre is issuing this alert to raise awareness of the vulnerabilities and associated reports of active exploitation.

Tracked as CVE-2026-88771 Footnote 3, this vulnerability is an Improper Input Validation vulnerability (CWE-20) Footnote 4. The vulnerability may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable NetScaler appliance. Successful exploitation could result in complete compromise of the appliance, unauthorized access to applications and services, credential theft, lateral movement, and further compromise of internal systems.

Tracked as CVE-2026-88772 Footnote 5, this vulnerability is a Buffer Overflow vulnerability (CWE-119) Footnote 6. Successful exploitation may allow arbitrary code execution, memory corruption, denial of service conditions, or other unintended behaviour on affected appliances.

Reports indicate that these vulnerabilities are being exploited and have been observed across multiple Citrix customer environments worldwide, although the full extent of this activity remains unknown at this time.

Beginning of Update 1

On October 2, 2026, Citrix published guidance Footnote 10 regarding a newly identified issue affecting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway deployments configured to use SAML authentication. According to Citrix, a remote attacker may be able to trigger system instability, resulting in denial-of-service conditions, repeated appliance reboots, and potentially further exploitation.

This issue is understood to be distinct from the vulnerabilities CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 described in the original alert.

The updates released to address CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 do not remediate this newly identified issue. Organizations using SAML authentication on NetScaler appliances should review their deployments, monitor for signs of abnormal activity, and follow the mitigation guidance provided by CitrixFootnote 10.

Additionally, organizations should be aware that patching alone may not fully remediate systems previously compromised through CVE-2026-88771 and/or CVE-2026-88772. If exploitation was successful, persistence mechanisms may remain on affected appliances even after the updates are applied. Organizations are strongly encouraged to run the NetScaler Console Indicators of Compromise (IOC) detection toolFootnote 11 to assess whether compromise has occurred and to contact Citrix for further instructions and remediation guidance.

End of Update 1

Beginning of Update 2

Another critical vulnerability has been discovered in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway environments configured as SAML Service Providers (SPs) or Identity Providers (IdPs)Footnote 12Footnote 13.

In response to the Citrix security bulletin released on October 8, 2026, the Cyber Centre issued AV26-1023 on October 9, 2026Footnote 14.

Tracked as CVE-2026-107406Footnote 15, this vulnerability is a memory overflow vulnerability (CWE-119)Footnote 6 leading to Denial of Service and potentially Remote Code Execution. Previous patches for the earlier vulnerabilities are insufficient to address this latest issue.

The Cyber Centre strongly recommends that affected organizations review the Citrix security bulletinFootnote 12 and update impacted NetScaler instances to the recommended versions as soon as possible.

End of Update 2

Suggested actions

Organizations should review the Citrix security bulletin Footnote 1 to determine whether their deployments are affected, prioritize remediation of Internet-facing systems, and investigate for signs of compromise, particularly where evidence of suspicious activity predates the release of vendor fixes

The Cyber Centre also recommends that organizations:

  • contact Citrix or their authorized support provider as soon as possible to obtain the latest security guidance and patch availability information
  • Preserve forensic evidence before shutting down, rebooting, patching, rebuilding, or otherwise modifying affected appliances, where feasible.
  • Preserve appliance logs, remote syslog records, and NetScaler Console logs.
  • Collect support bundles and other diagnostic information that may assist future investigations.
  • Review running processes and active network connections for suspicious or unexplained activity.
  • Examine startup scripts, scheduled tasks, web application directories, and crash dump locations for unauthorized modifications or indicators of persistence.
  • Preserve suspicious files and configurations before changing or removing them.
  • Correlate findings with firewall, DNS, authentication, endpoint, and other supporting telemetry sources.
  • Investigate unexpected outbound connections, unusual administrative access, and suspicious activity on connected systems.
  • Review the attached list of indicators of compromise and investigate to find matching patterns.
  • Follow Citrix guidance for suspected compromises, including isolation of affected appliances and assessment of credential exposure Footnote 7.
  • Conduct an organization-specific risk assessment based on the criticality of affected NetScaler deployments, any suspicious findings, and the limited information currently available.
  • Where operationally feasible and justified by the organization's risk assessment, consider temporarily disabling or shutting down Internet-facing NetScaler appliances until vendor guidance and security updates become available; organizations should carefully weigh the cybersecurity risks of continued operation against the operational and business impacts of service disruption before taking this action.
  • Prepare to reset credentials, invalidate active sessions, and replace certificates if compromise is suspected
  • Be prepared to rebuild or replace compromised appliances from trusted software and known-good configurations.

Note: Organizations operating Common Criteria Footnote 8 evaluated configurations should review Citrix's advisory Footnote 1 and apply the recommended updates in accordance with their change management and certification requirements.

In addition, the Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations review and implement the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security Actions Footnote 9.

  • Consolidate, monitor, and defend Internet gateways
  • Patch operating systems and applications
  • Harden operating systems and applications
  • Isolate web-facing applications

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.
